notes: An ICOCA card works on all trains. Kansai Airport is 40 minutes by Nankai Rapi:t. Nara and Kyoto are 45 minutes by Kintetsu or JR.
Summer brings 34°C heat and humidity. July has Tenjin Matsuri (fireworks on 25 July). Visit temples in the morning, and malls or the aquarium in the afternoon.
Osaka means kuidaore (eat until you drop): takoyaki, okonomiyaki and kushikatsu cost 500-1,500 JPY. Visit Kuromon in the morning.
For the USJ Nintendo area, book an area ticket in the app when the park opens. The Express Pass costs 10,000+ JPY.
Cash still matters, and 7-Eleven ATMs are handy. There is no tipping, and queues are silent.
Fushimi Inari is empty at 07:30. Tour buses arrive after 09:00.

transit.name: ICOCA
transit.why_chosen: It works on the Osaka Metro, JR and Hankyu, and is the same system as Suica.

stops.name: Osaka Castle
stops.tips: Toyotomi's castle: views from the 8th floor, a quiet park in the morning, cherry blossom in April.

stops.name: Osaka Castle Park
stops.tips: Parkland and moats around the castle, plus a plum grove.

stops.name: Kuromon Ichiba Market
stops.tips: Osaka's kitchen: eat standing at the stalls, with tuna, wagyu skewers and strawberries.

stops.name: Shinsaibashi-suji
stops.tips: A 600 m covered arcade with Don Quijote, drugstores and cosmetics.

stops.name: Dotonbori
stops.tips: The Glico running man and neon lights; try takoyaki (octopus balls) at Wanaka and okonomiyaki at Mizuno. Crowds line the canal.

backups.name: Mizuno Okonomiyaki
backups.tips: A Bib Gourmand okonomiyaki (savoury pancake) in Dotonbori, made with a yam batter.

backups.name: Tombori River Cruise
backups.tips: A 20-minute canal boat ride past the neon.

stops.name: Shitennoji Temple
stops.tips: Japan's oldest Buddhist temple (593), with a pagoda and garden.

stops.name: Shinsekai
stops.tips: A retro entertainment district with Tsutenkaku Tower and the Billiken statue.

stops.name: Tsutenkaku Tower
stops.tips: A tower from 1912, with an observation deck and a slide.

stops.name: Kushikatsu Daruma Shinsekai
stops.tips: Deep-fried skewers. Double-dipping in the sauce is forbidden.

stops.name: Abeno Harukas 300
stops.tips: The observation deck of Japan's tallest building, with views over Osaka and the sea.

backups.name: Yakko Kushikatsu
backups.tips: If Daruma is full, it's on the same street.

backups.name: Tennoji Park & Zoo
backups.tips: A park and zoo, as an alternative to Harukas.

stops.name: Nara Park
stops.tips: 40 minutes from Osaka on the Kintetsu line. 1,200 free-roaming deer, crackers for 200 JPY, quiet in the morning.

stops.name: Todai-ji
stops.tips: A 15 m Buddha inside the world's largest wooden building. Crawl through the hole in the pillar.

stops.name: Kasuga Taisha
stops.tips: A Shinto shrine with 3,000 stone lanterns, reached by a forest path.

stops.name: Nakatanidou Mochi
stops.tips: Watch the high-speed mochi pounding show and taste fresh yomogi (mugwort) mochi.

stops.name: Naramachi
stops.tips: A district of old merchant houses with cafes and crafts, and Nara's quieter side.

backups.name: Kamameshi Shizuka Nara
backups.tips: Rice cooked in an iron pot, for a hot lunch.

backups.name: Kofuku-ji
backups.tips: A five-storey pagoda, as an alternative to Naramachi.

stops.name: Umeda Sky Building
stops.tips: A floating garden observatory, clearest in the morning and among Kansai's best views.

stops.name: Nakanoshima Park
stops.tips: A park on an island between two rivers, with a rose garden and the City Hall.

stops.name: Osaka Nakanoshima Museum of Art
stops.tips: A black cube of a museum with Modigliani and Osaka art.

stops.name: Tenma Kisaburo
stops.tips: A local eatery in Tenma serving a daily teishoku (set meal).

stops.name: Tenjinbashisuji Shopping Street
stops.tips: Japan's longest covered shopping street (2.6 km), lined with local shops.

backups.name: Hanshin Department Store Snack Park
backups.tips: A standing-room food floor in Umeda. Try the ikayaki (grilled squid).

backups.name: Osaka Museum of Housing and Living
backups.tips: A recreated Edo-period street, with kimono rental.

stops.name: Fushimi Inari Taisha
stops.tips: 45 minutes from Osaka by JR. 10,000 red torii gates, empty at 07:30. Climb halfway up the mountain.

stops.name: Kiyomizu-dera
stops.tips: A temple with a wooden terrace, views over Kyoto and the streets of Higashiyama.

stops.name: Nishiki Market
stops.tips: Kyoto's kitchen: eat standing, with tsukemono (pickles) and tamagoyaki (rolled omelette).

stops.name: Gion
stops.tips: The geisha district, with Hanamikoji Street and Yasaka Shrine.

stops.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
stops.tips: A tunnel of bamboo. Crowds thin out in the late afternoon. Don't miss Togetsukyo Bridge.

backups.name: Kinkaku-ji
backups.tips: The Golden Pavilion, as an alternative to Arashiyama.

stops.name: Universal Studios Japan
stops.tips: Super Nintendo World (area tickets run out in the morning) and Harry Potter. A 1-Day Pass costs about 8,900 JPY, and the Express Pass is worth it on crowded days. Queue before the 08:30 opening.

stops.name: Universal CityWalk Osaka
stops.tips: Restaurants by the park exit, and a takoyaki museum.

stops.name: Tempozan Ferris Wheel
stops.tips: A Ferris wheel on Osaka Bay with night lights, 10 minutes from USJ.

backups.name: Kaiyukan Aquarium
backups.tips: An aquarium with a whale shark, as an alternative to USJ.

days.theme: Namba morning and a light farewell

stops.name: Namba Yasaka Shrine
stops.tips: A shrine with a stage built as a giant lion's head, good for photos.

stops.name: Hozenji Yokocho
stops.tips: Pour water over the moss-covered Fudo statue on a stone-paved lane.

stops.name: Wanaka Takoyaki Sennichimae
stops.tips: Osaka's classic takoyaki, for a farewell bite.

stops.name: Namba Parks
stops.tips: A canyon-shaped mall with a rooftop garden. Kansai Airport is 40 minutes away on the Nankai line.

backups.name: Ichiran Namba
backups.tips: Ramen, as an alternative to takoyaki.

backups.name: Kuromon Ichiba Morning Tour
backups.tips: The market at its morning best, good for souvenirs.
